THE SEED IDEA (from a Telegram brainstorm between the user, Alexander Didenko, and a friend — original Russian, translated):

- "Морской бой, в котором ты имеешь право переставлять корабли как угодно, если данные, которые ты сообщил при выстрелах врага остаются верными (попал, убил, мимо). И ты можешь это делать перед каждым выстрелом врага."
  => Battleship where the DEFENDER may rearrange their fleet arbitrarily between enemy shots, as long as every answer already given (hit / kill / miss) remains true of the new arrangement. Allowed before every enemy shot.
- "Понятно, что машина это легко сделает. Но вот человеку такая комбинаторика может быть сложна."
  => A machine can do this combinatorics trivially; a human cannot. (=> the game must do the combinatorics FOR the human player, and make it legible.)
- "это тоже будет восьмибитная игра" => it must be an 8-bit game.
- "тут идея в множественности реальностей" => the theme is multiplicity of realities.
- "у тебя есть двигатель Алькубьерре. Он не позволяет уйти ни в будущее ни в прошлое, но он позволяет по бране перейти в соседнюю версию реальности где космические корабли по другому стояли."
  => An Alcubierre drive: no time travel, but you can cross the BRANE into a neighbouring version of reality where the ships stood differently. (This is the in-fiction justification for rearranging.)
- "Лавкрафтовскую историю надо брать. Непознанный темный бог искажает реальность там, где ты ее не пришпилил."
  => Lovecraftian framing: an unknowable dark god twists reality wherever you have NOT pinned it down. (This is the perfect fictional statement of the core mechanic: unobserved = unfixed = hostile.)
- "Либо это битва с доктором Стрэнжем, который смотрит 14млн вариантов сценариев и выбирает нужный" (+ a Doctor Strange gif)
  => The 14,000,605 futures reference. Suggests a visible COUNTER of remaining consistent realities.
- "Смотри, каждая твоя перестановка открывает дорогу в мультивселенную" / "Но каждый мой выстрел накрывает корабли сразу во всех ветках!"
  => Every rearrangement opens a road into the multiverse; a shot lands in ALL branches at once.
- "есть особый снаряд которым я могу накрыть сразу несколько альтернативных веток"
  => a special munition that covers several alternative branches at once.
- Warhammer 40k GELLER FIELD was raised: "Генераторы поля создают вокруг корабля почти невидимую энергетическую завесу — своеобразный пузырь реальности. Внутри этого пузыря продолжают действовать законы физического пространства-времени, а не хаотичные и извращённые правила Имматериума."
  => A bubble of STABLE reality. Obvious mechanic: project it onto a region and reality inside is PINNED — cannot shift any more. Literally "пришпилить реальность".
- Working title floated by the friend: "Рыцари и лжецы в мультивселенной безумия" (Knights and Liars in the Multiverse of Madness).
- The user's verdict on the state of the idea: "короче надо докрутить" (needs finishing/tightening).

WHAT THE USER ASKED FOR NOW (verbatim):
"Мне нужна новая 8битная игра. Я вообще без понятия как ты ее сделаешь и в каком лоре. Но она должна быть такая же крутая как десант Nostromo."
=> A new 8-bit game, lore is my call, it must be as cool as the Nostromo landing game (the existing project 'nostromo-gambit'). The user then said: work maximally autonomously, they are going to sleep. So: NO questions can be asked. Make confident decisions and justify them.

MY WORKING DIRECTION (challenge it if it is wrong, but this is the frame):
The player is the ATTACKER hunting a fleet that exists in superposition. The enemy fleet is not "hidden" — it is genuinely UNDETERMINED, collapsing only where the player has pinned it. The HUD's centrepiece is a big counter of remaining consistent realities, ticking down from millions. The visual signature is GHOST FLEETS: faint flickering silhouettes of sampled possible placements drawn over the enemy grid, converging into solid hulls as the possibility space collapses. Symmetrically, the PLAYER's own fleet also evades — the machine does that combinatorics for the human — but evading costs a resource and feeds the dark god.

CONSTRAINT: the deliverable must be a finished, polished, self-contained 8-bit game of the same production quality and scale as the existing 'nostromo-gambit' project. Not a prototype, not a toy. It must be genuinely fun to a human, not just conceptually clever.



=== REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (nostromo-gambit — the quality bar) ===
Path: G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\nostromo-gambit  — this is a MIRROR (source-only, no node_modules). The LIVE, runnable working copy is C:\dev\nostromo-gambit. They are byte-identical except (a) C: has one extra file scripts\mutation-check.mjs, (b) C:\dev\...\public\app.js is 3 lines newer (a banner-phase reset). Sync direction is C: -> G: via `npm run mirror` (scripts/mirror-to-drive.mjs). NEVER run npm install on G:.
Stack: NO BUILD TOOLING AT ALL. No bundler, no transpiler, no framework, no CSS preprocessor, no TypeScript, no test framework package.

- Runtime: Node >= 22, `"type": "module"`, plain ESM `.mjs` everywhere on the server.
- Exactly ONE npm dependency in the whole project: `"chess.js": "1.4.0"`. Zero devDependencies. Tests run on the built-in `node --test`.
- Server: raw `node:http` + a hand-written 9-route router (src/server/http.mjs), a hand-written static file server (src/server/static.mjs) and a hand-written SSE hub (src/server/sse.mjs). Comment at the top of http.mjs: "Маршрутизатор на node:http. Никаких фреймворков — маршрутов девять."
- Client: three plain ES modules loaded with `<script type="module" src="/app.js">`, no imports from any CDN, no npm packages on the front end. `public/app.js` uses top-level `await` (it is a module).
- Rendering: NOT canvas. NOT React. Plain DOM + CSS transforms + inline SVG generated in JS. Board = 64 permanent `<div class="sq">` in a CSS grid + a separate absolutely-positioned `.pieces` layer where each piece is a `<div class="piece">` moved by `transform: translate(%,%)`.
- Transport: one GET /api/state + one SSE stream GET /api/events + five POST endpoints. No WebSocket.
- External engine: official Stockfish binary, downloaded at setup time into %LOCALAPPDATA%, driven as a SEPARATE PROCESS over UCI (deliberate weak coupling for GPL reasons). Not bundled, not in the repo.
- Zero external assets: no image files, no font files, no audio files, no icon files. The favicon is an inline `data:image/svg+xml` in index.html.
- package.json scripts: setup / start / test / test:unit / test:real / selfplay / audit / e2e / mirror / bench.
- .npmrc pins the npm cache to C: (`cache=C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\npm-cache`, `fund=false`, `audit=false`).
Scale: ~6149 lines of game code.
Files: Runtime game code = 6,149 lines (src 4,215 + public 1,934). Shipped total including tests and tooling = 8,857 lines of code + 350 lines of Russian docs.

public/ — 1,934 lines, THE PART THE NEW GAME MOST NEEDS TO MATCH
  theme.css        571 lines / 18.3 KB  — the entire 8-bit CRT look
  app.js           547 lines / 22.2 KB  — event stream, rendering, input, start screen
  sprites.js       410 lines / 11.4 KB  — 16x16 ASCII bitmaps -> SVG
  board.js         226 lines /  9.4 KB  — 64 squares, piece diffing, pointer input
  index.html       180 lines /  8.7 KB  — full static skeleton, every panel pre-declared

src/ — 4,215 lines
  game/dropGenerator.mjs 474  game/fen.mjs 282  game/dropRules.mjs 251
  game/marginal.mjs 222  game/game.mjs 356  game/packages.mjs 166
  game/sharpness.mjs 121  game/storytellers.mjs 107  game/computer.mjs 76
  game/rng.mjs 76  game/dice.mjs 51  game/fischer.mjs 60
  engine/uci.mjs 407  engine/pool.mjs 277  engine/evaluate.mjs 166
  engine/registry.mjs 145  engine/mock.mjs 141  engine/analysis.mjs 123
  server/main.mjs 360  server/http.mjs 115  server/sse.mjs 114  server/static.mjs 56
  shared/paths.mjs 69

scripts/ — 1,053 lines
  get-stockfish.mjs 471, selfplay.mjs 305, bench-drops.mjs 139, corpus.mjs 66,
  mirror-to-drive.mjs 60, stockfish.lock.json 12  (+ mutation-check.mjs on C: only)

test/ — 1,655 lines, 118 tests, all green in ~14 s
  unit/*.test.mjs (7 files, 101 tests) run against an in-process MockEngine so they
  finish in seconds; integration/http.test.mjs (229 lines, 17 tests) boots the REAL
  server on port 0 and parses raw SSE frames; helpers/server.mjs 112;
  fixtures/fake-engine.mjs 156; e2e/serve-for-e2e.mjs 35.

Docs: README.md 169 lines, REPORT.md 181 lines — both in Russian, both written as prose
for the user (not for a machine), both include a "known limitations / what was NOT done"
section. Matching that documentation standard is part of the quality bar.
Aesthetic: "Ship's terminal": green phosphor vs amber phosphor on near-black, scanlines, vignette, brightness flicker. Every pixel is CSS or generated SVG — comment at the top of theme.css: "Всё рисуется CSS — ни одной картинки, ни одного внешнего шрифта."

PALETTE (public/theme.css :root, exact hex):
  --phosphor:       #7dff9b   green phosphor = side 1 (marines / white)
  --phosphor-dim:   #3d8a52   secondary text, borders on buttons
  --phosphor-faint: #1c3d27   tertiary text, coordinates, "nothing here yet"
  --amber:          #ffb347   amber phosphor = side 2 (xenos / black), all warnings
  --amber-dim:      #8a5f26
  --alert:          #ff4d4d   only for the broken-link dot
  --bg:             #050a06   page ground
  --panel:          #0a140c   panel fill
  --panel-edge:     #16301c   every 1px border, every separator
  --light-square:   #17301d
  --dark-square:    #0d1e11
Literal one-off colors: check square background #3a0f0f; eval-bar label text #dfffe8 on
rgba(5,10,6,0.78); overlay scrim rgba(5,10,6,0.9); glow shadows are
rgba(125,255,155,0.x) for green and rgba(255,179,71,0.x) for amber.

SPRITE PALETTE (public/sprites.js, per side, 4 colors each):
  w: { x:'#06170c'  outline, '#':'#7dff9b' body, o:'#dcffe6' highlight, '*':'#ffd166' accent }
  b: { x:'#1d0f00'  outline, '#':'#ffb347' body, o:'#ffe3ba' highlight, '*':'#b6ff5a' accent }
Doctrine stated in the file: the two sides differ by HUE, not by brightness, so they stay
legible on a dim CRT — and both hues are real period monitor phosphors.

FONT: `--font: 'Consolas', 'DejaVu Sans Mono', 'Courier New', monospace;` — system mono
only, no webfont, no @font-face, nothing loaded from Google Fonts. Body 14px,
`letter-spacing: 0.04em`. Titles are wide-tracked uppercase: `.title` 17px/0.22em,
`.start-title` 25px/0.3em, panel `<h2>` 11px/0.2em, buttons 12px/0.12em.
Text-shadow glow on titles only: `0 0 8px rgba(125,255,155,0.5)` / `0 0 14px …0.45`.

SPRITE TECHNIQUE (this is the signature move, copy it verbatim):
16 rows x 16 chars of ASCII, one string per row, 4 symbols: `.` transparent, `x` outline,
`#` body, `o` highlight, `*` accent. `spriteSvg()` walks each row, run-length-merges
horizontally identical pixels into one `<rect>`, and emits
`<svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" shape-rendering="crispEdges" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">`.
Results are memoized in a `Map` keyed `set:color:type`. The RLE is not decoration — the
comment says without it the board would cost >4000 DOM nodes in pieces alone.
Two full sets exist: `classic` (traditional silhouettes) and `xeno` (marines vs xenomorphs),
switchable at runtime from the settings drawer.

RESOLUTION / SCALING: there is no fixed canvas. Board is `--board-max: min(72vh, 560px)`
(mobile: `min(92vw, 520px)`), squares are a `repeat(8,1fr)` grid, each piece is
`width:12.5%; height:12.5%` with `.piece svg { padding: 7%; image-rendering: pixelated }`.
So a 16x16 bitmap renders at ~65px and stays crisp via crispEdges + pixelated.

CRT EFFECT — one pseudo-element over everything, click-through:
  body::after { position:fixed; inset:0; pointer-events:none; z-index:100;
    background:
      repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(0,0,0,.22) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
      radial-gradient(ellipse at center, transparent 55%, rgba(0,0,0,.55) 100%);
    animation: flicker 5.5s infinite steps(60); }
`steps(60)` is what makes the flicker read as a CRT and not as a fade. The flicker
keyframes only dip at 97%/99% (0.93 / 0.96) — subtle, never distracting.

MOTION VOCABULARY (exact durations — reuse these numbers, they are tuned):
  piece move          transform 180ms ease-out (piece never re-created, only translated)
  drop landing        340ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), starts 44px above with
                      scale(1.7) and opacity 0 — overshoot reads as a LANDING
  shockwave ring      460ms ease-out, scale(0.2)->2.2, opacity .7->0, amber border
  banner slide        translateY(-100%) -> 0, 220ms ease-out
  drawer slide        translateX(100%) -> 0, 200ms ease-out
  eval bar            height/width 260ms ease-out
  toast               opacity+translateY 200ms, auto-hides after 3400ms
  die shake           90ms infinite ±1px/±4deg; spin redraws every 70ms for 700ms
  boot typewriter     9ms per character, 120ms per line break
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` appears THREE times and kills the flicker, the
piece transition, the landing animation and the shockwave. Non-negotiable for parity.

LAYOUT: one CSS grid with named areas —
  grid-template-areas: 'head head head' / 'evalbar board side' / 'foot foot foot'
  grid-template-columns: 42px var(--board-max) minmax(300px, 1fr)
  max-width 1240px, `overflow:hidden` on html/body (desktop), gap 12px, padding 10px 14px.
At `max-width: 980px` it collapses to a single column, areas reorder to
'head' 'evalbar' 'board' 'foot' 'side', and the vertical eval bar becomes a horizontal
22px strip whose gradient direction flips. Note the file ends with a DUPLICATED narrow
media block and an explicit comment explaining that a later `.foot { flex-wrap: nowrap }`
rule won on equal specificity, so the mobile rules had to be repeated last. That kind of
comment — the fix plus why — is the house style.

CHROME DETAILS worth copying: 1px `--panel-edge` borders on everything; panel headers are
11px 0.2em uppercase dim-green on a bordered strip; buttons are transparent with a dim
border and hover = 10% tint + 8px glow; segmented controls (`.seg`) collapse borders with
`border-right-width:0` except `:last-child`, and the active one gets
`inset 0 0 10px rgba(125,255,155,.18)`; dice are 3x3 CSS grids of 5px round `<i>` pips;
`.pips` uses `●●●○○` text characters for remaining rolls; separators in the move log are
`border-top: 1px dashed var(--amber-dim)` with the text `═══ ДЕСАНТ #3 ═══`.
Audio: THERE IS NO AUDIO. NONE. I grepped the entire project (both the G: mirror and the C: live copy) for AudioContext / createOscillator / webkitAudioContext / `new Audio(` / sound / звук / audio — zero matches. There is no audio engine, no chiptune player, no sound file, no mute toggle, no volume setting, no `<audio>` element, no gesture-unlock code.

This is the single biggest gap in the reference project and the clearest place where the second game can EXCEED the bar rather than merely match it. Do not go looking for a helper to copy — there is nothing. If the new game wants sound, it must be written from scratch.

Constraints the new audio code must respect to stay consistent with the project's doctrine:
1. Zero external assets and zero dependencies. That rules out sample files and audio libraries; it means WebAudio synthesis (oscillators + gain envelopes + a noise buffer) written by hand, the same way sprites are hand-generated rather than shipped as PNGs.
2. Autoplay policy: nostromo-gambit has an explicit first-click gate already available — the `#start-go` "▶ НАЧАТЬ ОПЕРАЦИЮ" button on the start screen is guaranteed to be a user gesture. That is where `new AudioContext()` should be created / resumed.
3. It must honour the same accessibility instinct as `prefers-reduced-motion`: an audio on/off checkbox belongs in the settings drawer next to "Показывать шкалу оценки", persisted through the same settings POST, and it must default in a way that never surprises.
4. Every sound needs a named, motivated trigger the same way every animation does — the existing event vocabulary gives the hook points for free: `move`, `drop:start`, `drop:progress`, `drop:done`, `drop:skipped`, `dice`, `thinking`, check, game over, boot typewriter keyclick.
5. Palette discipline translates to audio: two timbres for the two sides (green/amber), one alert timbre, nothing else — the same "two hues, not two brightnesses" logic.
Architecture: SHAPE: a local single-player-at-one-screen web app with an authoritative Node server. The client is deliberately stupid. Top of public/app.js, verbatim:

  // Клиент намеренно ничего не решает сам: легальность ходов, расписание десанта
  // и счёт жетонов живут на сервере и приходят готовыми. Здесь только три вещи —
  // отрисовка, ввод указателя и тайминги анимаций.

THERE IS NO GAME LOOP. No requestAnimationFrame, no setInterval tick, no fixed timestep,
no update()/draw() split anywhere in the project. The app is 100% event-driven: server
state changes -> SSE frame -> `applyState(next)` -> full re-render of a small DOM. All
motion is delegated to CSS transitions/animations. The only timers in the client are the
dice spin (`setInterval(…, 70)` for 700 ms), the boot typewriter (chained `setTimeout`),
the toast dismissal (3400 ms) and shockwave cleanup (500 ms). If the second game needs a
real-time loop, that pattern must be invented — there is nothing here to copy.

SERVER STATE MACHINE — `class Game` (src/game/game.mjs), 356 lines:
  phase: 'idle' | 'dropping' | 'over'   (set in #refreshGameOver)
  version: monotonically incremented on EVERY mutation; it is both the SSE event id and
           the optimistic-concurrency token.
  Own journal instead of the library's: `atoms[]` (each `{kind:'move'|'drop', …}`) plus a
  parallel `snapshots[]` stack of FENs. Reason is documented at the top of the file —
  chess.js 1.4.0 `load()` calls `clear()` and destroys its own history, and the drop
  mechanic must rebuild the position from FEN, so undo/move-list/threefold would have
  silently vanished. There is a regression test for exactly this.
  Stable piece identity: `this.pieces` is a Map square -> `{id:'p17', type, color}`.
  IDs are assigned from a module-level `nextPieceId` counter and are what makes the client
  animate instead of blink. `#applyPieceMove(m)` transfers the id using the SEMANTICS of
  the move (en-passant victim square, castling rook hop, promotion type swap) because you
  cannot infer identity by diffing two positions.
  Honest degradation: after undo, ids are re-issued (`#rebuildPieceIds`) and the board
  redraws wholesale, with a comment saying this is more honest than pretending.

APP ORCHESTRATOR — `class App` (src/server/main.mjs), 360 lines: owns sessionId (randomUUID),
Game, SseHub, EnginePool, AnalysisEngine, Rng, and the `dropInProgress` / `dropAbort` pair.
Async work (computer move, drop search) is deliberately NOT awaited inside the HTTP handler:

  // Намеренно не await: ход считается в фоне, а состояние уезжает клиенту событием.
  // Иначе HTTP-ответ на ход человека ждал бы, пока движок додумает свой…

and every background task re-checks `this.game.version !== versionAtStart` before applying
its result, because the game may have been reset/undone while it was thinking.

SCREENS (there are no routes; screens are stacked z-indexed overlays in one HTML file):
  .start   z-index 90  full-screen start card, `.off` hides it
  .drawer  z-index 60  settings, slides in from the right
  .overlay z-index 50  two of them: game-over card and promotion picker; `.on` shows
  .toast   z-index 70  transient message
  body::after z-index 100 CRT layer above everything, pointer-events none
The start screen is shown ONLY when there is nothing to resume — last 8 lines of app.js:
`const gameInProgress = state && (state.moveLog.length > 0 || state.dropLog.length > 0)`;
if resuming it shows the toast «ПАРТИЯ ВОССТАНОВЛЕНА» instead. This exists because a
reload mid-game used to cover a live board with a screen whose only button would erase it.

HTTP API (src/server/http.mjs): GET /api/state, GET /api/events, GET /health,
POST /api/move | /api/roll | /api/new-game | /api/undo | /api/settings,
POST /api/_test/fen (only when NODE_ENV=test). One `STATUS` table maps error codes to
HTTP statuses (409 for conflicts, 422 for illegal move, 503 for engine down). Body limit
64 KB. Errors are caught so a bad request never kills a game in progress.

OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY: client sends `version: state.version` with move/roll/undo; a
mismatch returns `{code:'STALE_VERSION'}` and the client treats it as non-error and just
re-reads state (`if (data.code === 'STALE_VERSION') { await refresh(); return data; }`).

EVENT STREAM: exactly ONE multiplexed SSE endpoint, with the reason spelled out — HTTP/1.1
allows ~6 connections per origin, two streams x two tabs already eats four. Event names:
`snapshot`, `state`, `move`, `settings` (all carry a full snapshot and an `id:`),
plus volatile `eval`, `thinking`, `drop:progress` (NO `id:`, so they cannot poison
Last-Event-ID), plus `dice`, `drop:start`, `drop:done`, `drop:skipped`.
A 200-frame ring buffer replays from Last-Event-ID; if there is a gap it falls back to a
full snapshot. 15 s heartbeat comments, `retry: 3000`, `setNoDelay(true)` (Nagle was
batching 60-byte eval frames into 40 ms jerks), `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, `no-transform`.

INPUT (public/board.js `#bindPointer`): Pointer Events only — NOT HTML5 drag&drop, with
the reason in a comment (ghost image, no touch support, no control over animation). Two
interaction modes on the same handler: drag (pointerdown -> capture -> pointermove sets
`transform` in px -> pointerup hit-tests) and click-click (select source, then click a
highlighted target). `#squareFromPoint(x,y)` converts client coords via
`getBoundingClientRect()` and a /8 floor. On release the piece is ALWAYS snapped back
locally and the server's echo is what actually moves it. `board.setLocked()` freezes input
during a drop and after game over. `.board { touch-action: none; user-select: none }`.
Keyboard: only `Escape` (closes drawer + promo, clears selection).

PERSISTENCE: there is none on the client — no localStorage, no cookies, no save file.
State lives in server memory; a page reload re-fetches it. Runtime artifacts (engine
binary, selfplay NDJSON, PID registry) live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nostromo-gambit\` via
src/shared/paths.mjs, deliberately NOT next to the sources, because the source folder is
on a Google Drive virtual volume. `writeJsonAtomic()` = write .tmp then rename.

DETERMINISM: `makeRng(seed)` (xorshift128+) everywhere; `Math.random` appears exactly once
in the whole client and only to spin the dice faces visually. Same seed reproduces the
whole game including the Fischer start position (`fischerFen(makeRng('fischer:'+seed))`).
Reusable helpers: Verbatim signatures of the helpers worth lifting into the second game.

PIXEL-ART RENDERER (public/sprites.js) — the highest-value single function:
  export const PALETTES = { w: {...}, b: {...} }          // 4 keys: x # o *
  export function spriteSvg(setName, color, type) -> string   // memoized, RLE'd SVG
  export const PIECE_LETTER = { p:'П', n:'К', b:'С', r:'Л', q:'Ф', k:'Кр' }
  export const PIECE_NAME   = { p:'пешка', ... }
Generalize by renaming `setName/color/type` to `(setName, paletteKey, spriteKey)` and
keeping the ASCII-bitmap-as-string-array authoring format unchanged.

BOARD / SPRITE LAYER (public/board.js) — a reusable "grid of cells + diffed sprite layer":
  export function squareName(file, rank)
  export class BoardView {
    constructor({ squaresEl, piecesEl, boardEl, onSelect })
    render(board, { legalMoves = {}, lastMove = null, checkSquare = null,
                    reinforced = [], landedIds = null } = {})
    select(sq); clearSelection();
    shockwave(squares);                  // spawns .shock spans, self-removing after 500ms
    setLocked(locked); setPieceSet(name, badges);
    #buildSquares(); #bindPointer(); #squareFromPoint(x, y); #placePiece(el, square);
    #createPiece(p);
  }
The load-bearing idea to copy: cells are built ONCE and never re-created; entities live in
a sibling absolutely-positioned layer, are keyed by a server-assigned stable id, and are
moved with `--tx/--ty` custom properties + `transform: translate(var(--tx), var(--ty))`.
That one decision is what turns "re-render" into "animation".

TOAST (public/app.js) — 6 lines, uses a property on the function itself as the timer slot:
  function toast(text) { el.toast.textContent = text; el.toast.classList.add('on');
    clearTimeout(toast.t); toast.t = setTimeout(() => el.toast.classList.remove('on'), 3400); }

TYPEWRITER BOOT SEQUENCE (public/app.js):

HONESTY AS A DESIGN PRINCIPLE. This is the strongest through-line and the thing that makes
the project feel expensive. When something cannot be done properly it is disabled and said
out loud, in the UI, not hidden: Fischer castling is off and the start screen says so;
a failed drop refunds the die and prints the reason; a widened tolerance is written into
the drop log as «ДОПУСК РАСШИРЕН ДО ±45 СП»; undo after a drop admits it must redraw the
whole board. README and REPORT both end with «Известные ограничения» / «Что осталось
несделанным». The second game must have that section too.

OPENING. Not a splash screen — a configuration terminal, exactly like an era game. The
boot text types itself character by character (9 ms/char, 120 ms/line) above the title,
then a single card asks EVERYTHING at once via segmented buttons: player 1 human/computer,
player 2 human/computer, computer level 1–5, planner, start position, dice rolls per
player, auto-drop frequency. Every option has a live one-line explanatory note under it
(`.opt-note`, amber-dim) that changes as you select — the level note, the planner blurb,
the Fischer caveat. One amber call-to-action: «▶ НАЧАТЬ ОПЕРАЦИЮ». Under it, one honest
line about the 32-piece ceiling.

DIFFICULTY. Five named levels with character, not numbers: 1 РЯДОВОЙ / 2 КАПРАЛ /
3 СЕРЖАНТ / 4 ЛЕЙТЕНАНТ / 5 MU-TH-UR 6000 («Полная сила на этой машине. Удачи.»).
Default is 3. Crucially, weakening is done by MultiPV move selection within a `slackCp`
window (220/130/60/20/0), NOT by cutting depth — with the stated reason: a depth-starved
engine plays *stranger*, not weaker; it still never blunders two-move tactics but stops
having a plan. Even level 1 is forbidden from gifting a queen.

PACING. Turn-based, no timers, no pressure. The drama is manufactured in two places:
(1) the drop — a banner slides down over the board, the board dims to 0.55 and goes
`cursor:wait`, a phase-weighted progress bar advances through four named phases
(weights 0.05/0.2/0.55/1.0 so the bar never lies about which stage it is in), and it ends
with pieces falling from above with an overshoot plus amber shockwave rings and a toast;
(2) the dice — 700 ms of shaking, faces reshuffling every 70 ms, then the readout line
that tells you exactly what you bought. Search takes 4–6 s in practice and REPORT.md says
plainly that this was over the 2.5 s target — the progress bar with meaningful phase names
is the accepted mitigation: "ожидание читается как работа, а не как зависание."

WHAT MAKES IT FEEL GOOD. (a) Nothing ever blinks: stable piece ids mean every change is a
motion. (b) Every number shown is explained somewhere — the drop log prints
`+0.34 → +0.29 · Δ -5 сп · ЦЕЛЬ 0 · 4.2 с` and the header prints the hold count.
(c) Personality lives in tables, not in code branches — three "planners" (МАТЬ / БИШОП /
ЭШ, borrowed conceptually from RimWorld storytellers) differ only by weights and tolerance,
each with a `tone: { start, done, skipped }` string triple; ЭШ's line is
«ВЫСАДКА ВЫПОЛНЕНА. НЕ МОГУ ЛГАТЬ О ВАШИХ ШАНСАХ.». (d) Tension is built into the dice
math rather than into UI noise: sum buys tonnage, spread buys bias, and a double gives max
tonnage with ZERO bias while 6–1 gives max bias with almost no tonnage — you cannot have
both. (e) The one aesthetic ruling the user made mid-build is recorded in REPORT.md and
worth internalizing: the eval bar used to be "green vs empty", which speaks the language of
white and black; it was recolored to green-vs-amber so it speaks the language of THIS
game's two sides.

ENDING. A centered card over a 0.9 scrim: the reason in huge tracked caps («МАТ»), one
statistics line («Ходов: 47 · Десантов: 6 · Фигур на доске: 21»), and two buttons —
«НОВАЯ ПАРТИЯ» (returns to the configuration terminal, never straight into a game) and
«ПОСМОТРЕТЬ ПАРТИЮ» (dismisses the card so you can study the final position). There is also
`Game.toPgn()` which exports the game with drops as PGN comments, so a game can be re-read.

//   .  прозрачно      x  контур       #  тело
//   o  блик           *  акцент (визор морпеха, кислота ксеноморфа)

export const PALETTES = {
  w: { x: '#06170c', '#': '#7dff9b', o: '#dcffe6', '*': '#ffd166' },
  b: { x: '#1d0f00', '#': '#ffb347', o: '#ffe3ba', '*': '#b6ff5a' },
};

const cache = new Map();

/**
 * Разворачивает битмап в SVG. Соседние пиксели одного цвета склеиваются в один
 * прямоугольник по горизонтали: без этого на доску уходило бы больше четырёх тысяч
 * узлов DOM только под фигуры.
 */
export function spriteSvg(setName, color, type) {
  const key = `${setName}:${color}:${type}`;
  if (cache.has(key)) return cache.get(key);

  const set = SETS[setName] || SETS.xeno;
  const rows = (set[color] || set.w)[type] || CLASSIC[type];
  const palette = PALETTES[color];
  const parts = [];

  for (let y = 0; y < rows.length; y++) {
    const row = rows[y];
    let x = 0;
    while (x < row.length) {
      const ch = row[x];
      if (ch === '.' || ch === ' ') { x += 1; continue; }
      let run = 1;
      while (x + run < row.length && row[x + run] === ch) run += 1;
      const fill = palette[ch] || palette['#'];
      parts.push(`<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${run}" height="1" fill="${fill}"/>`);
      x += run;
    }

  /**
   * Указатель, а не нативный drag&drop: последний тащит призрачную картинку,
   * не работает на касании и не даёт управлять анимацией. Плюс поддержан
   * режим «клик по источнику — клик по цели», которым играет большинство.
   */
  #bindPointer() {
    let dragging = null;

    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointerdown', (ev) => {
      if (this.locked) return;
      const sq = this.#squareFromPoint(ev.clientX, ev.clientY);
      if (!sq) return;

      // Второй клик по подсвеченной цели завершает ход.
      if (this.selected && this.legalMoves[this.selected]?.includes(sq)) {
        this.onSelect({ from: this.selected, to: sq });
        this.clearSelection();
        return;
      }

      const piece = this.board.find((p) => p.square === sq);
      if (!piece || !this.legalMoves[sq]) { this.clearSelection(); return; }

      this.select(sq);
      const el = this.pieceEls.get(piece.id);
      if (!el) return;
      dragging = { from: sq, el, pointerId: ev.pointerId, moved: false };
      el.classList.add('dragging');
      this.boardEl.setPointerCapture(ev.pointerId);
      ev.preventDefault();
    });

    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointermove', (ev) => {
      if (!dragging) return;
      const rect = this.boardEl.getBoundingClientRect();
      const size = rect.width / 8;
      const x = ev.clientX - rect.left - size / 2;
      const y = ev.clientY - rect.top - size / 2;
      dragging.moved = true;
      dragging.el.style.transform = `translate(${x}px, ${y}px)`;
    });

    const finish = (ev) => {
      if (!dragging) return;
      const { from, el, moved } = dragging;
      dragging = null;
      el.classList.remove('dragging');
      el.style.transform = '';
      this.#placePiece(el, from); // вернём на место; сервер подтвердит настоящий ход
      try { this.boardEl.releasePointerCapture(ev.pointerId); } catch { /* захват мог уже отпуститься сам */ }
      if (!moved) return; // это был обычный клик — выбор уже сделан
      const to = this.#squareFromPoint(ev.clientX, ev.clientY);
      if (!to || to === from) return;
      if (!this.legalMoves[from]?.includes(to)) return;
      this.onSelect({ from, to });
      this.clearSelection();
    };

    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointerup', finish);
    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointercancel', finish);
  }

  #squareFromPoint(x, y) {
    const rect = this.boardEl.getBoundingClientRect();
    const f = Math.floor(((x - rect.left) / rect.width) * 8);
    const r = 8 - Math.floor(((y - rect.top) / rect.height) * 8);
    if (f < 0 || f > 7 || r < 1 || r > 8) return null;
    return squareName(f, r);
  }

export class Rng {
  constructor(seed = 'nostromo') {
    this.seed = String(seed);
    const [a, b, c, d] = hashSeed(seed);
    this.s = new Uint32Array([a, b, c, d]);
    // Прокручиваем, чтобы близкие сиды не давали похожих первых чисел.
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) this.next();
  }
  next() {                                   // xorshift128+, uint32
    let t = this.s[3]; const s0 = this.s[0];
    this.s[3] = this.s[2]; this.s[2] = this.s[1]; this.s[1] = s0;
    t ^= t << 11; t ^= t >>> 8;
    this.s[0] = (t ^ s0 ^ (s0 >>> 19)) >>> 0;
    return this.s[0];
  }
  float() { return this.next() / 4294967296; }
  int(min, max) { if (max < min) return min; return min + (this.next() % (max - min + 1)); }
  pick(arr) { if (!arr || arr.length === 0) return undefined; return arr[this.next() % arr.length]; }
  shuffle(arr) { for (let i = arr.length - 1; i > 0; i--) { const j = this.next() % (i + 1); [arr[i], arr[j]] = [arr[j], arr[i]]; } return arr; }
  weighted(items, weightOf = (x) => x.weight) {
    const total = items.reduce((s, x) => s + Math.max(0, weightOf(x)), 0);
    if (total <= 0) return this.pick(items);
    let roll = this.float() * total;
    for (const item of items) { roll -= Math.max(0, weightOf(item)); if (roll <= 0) return item; }
    return items[items.length - 1];
  }
  /** Отдельный поток случайности, привязанный к метке — чтобы ветки не сдвигали друг друга. */
  fork(label) { return new Rng(`${this.seed}:${label}:${this.next()}`); }
}
export function makeRng(seed) { return new Rng(seed); }

Here is a design proposal for the game (angle: mechanic):

<<<PROPOSAL>>>
# ГАМБИТ АЗАТОТА — SYSTEMS RULESET v1.0

Working title: **«ГАМБИТ АЗАТОТА»** (series-mate to NOSTROMO GAMBIT). Subtitle: «МОРСКОЙ БОЙ В НЕЗАКРЕПЛЁННОЙ РЕАЛЬНОСТИ · БОЕВОЙ МОДУЛЬ». Lovecraft frame (blind idiot god twists what you have not pinned) over 40k hardware (Geller field) and Alcubierre brane-crossing. Adopted, not negotiable below.

---

## 0. THE ONE IDEA THE WHOLE DESIGN COLLAPSES INTO

Neither fleet is ever placed. Both fleets are **possibility sets**: the set of all placements consistent with every answer given so far. There is no hidden truth to be found — there is only a set that shrinks. Therefore:

**N == 1 ⟺ every ship's placement is determined ⟺ that fleet is destroyed.**

"Sink all four ships" and "collapse the counter to one" are the *same condition*, provably. This is the design's mechanical purity: there is exactly one win condition, it is a number, it is on screen at all times, and both sides have one. The HUD centrepiece is two counters racing down from ~25 000 000 to 1. Everything else in this document is machinery for buying and spending **bits**.

---

## 1. BOARD AND FLEET

1.1 Two 8×8 boards, files А–З (Cyrillic) or A–H, ranks 1–8. Enemy board is the large centre board; own board is a smaller panel on the right. Attention asymmetry mirrors agency asymmetry.

1.2 Fleet, both sides, identical: **4, 3, 3, 2** — four ships, 12 cells of 64 (18.75%).

1.3 Ships may touch. Stated in the rules panel: «КОРАБЛИ МОГУТ КАСАТЬСЯ — ЭТО РАСШИРЯЕТ МУЛЬТИВЕРСУМ». Forbidding contact would shrink the space ~4× and hand out free deduction on every kill; this game already gives free deduction (§6.3) and needs the space large.

1.4 Two ships of equal length are indistinguishable, so configurations are counted with the 3-ships divided by 2!.

1.5 Placement counts: L=4 → 80, L=3 → 96, L=2 → 112. Upper bound 80·96·96·112/2 = **41 287 680**; after removing overlaps the true count is ≈24–27 M. **Hardcode the exact number as a constant, print it during the boot typewriter («ПЕРЕПИСЬ ВЕТВЕЙ ......... 24 9XX XXX»), and have a unit test recompute it by full DFS.** Constant + test + honest boot line is the house style.

1.6 Why 4 ships and not 5: five ships puts the space at ~10⁹, which is neither exactly enumerable at boot nor winnable in under 35 turns. 12 target cells out of 64 gives an 18–24 turn match. A 10×10 / five-ship «ГЛУБОКАЯ ВОДА» variant is explicitly **cut from v1** and listed under «что не сделано».

---

## 2. THE DEFENDER (the god's answering rule)

2.1 A fleet's state is *only* its constraint set: `E` (cells answered empty), `H` (cells answered hit), `SUNK` (ships pinned to an exact placement), `GELLER` (region → exact occupied count). A configuration is *consistent* iff it satisfies all of them. N = |consistent set|.

2.2 **Answering a salvo S (k cells) requires ONE configuration.** The defender selects the consistent configuration P minimising, in strict lexicographic order:
 (a) |P ∩ S| — hits taken;
 (b) number of ships of P fully contained in H ∪ S — kills taken;
 (c) −(resulting N) — remaining freedom, maximised;
 (d) seeded tie-break.
Then it reports the per-cell result of P, and the constraints are extended.

2.3 **A salvo of k cells is strictly stronger than k sequential shots.** Sequentially, the defender dodges each cell independently and will essentially never be hit before the board is saturated. Simultaneously, it must satisfy all k with one reality. This asymmetry *is* the game's core skill lever, so the salvo is not an option — it is the only offensive verb (§4).

2.4 **A hit does not name a ship.** Report is «ПОПАДАНИЕ», nothing more. Ship identity is itself in superposition: a hit cell may be re-attributed to a different ship in a later configuration, provided all constraints hold. On a forced kill the report is «УНИЧТОЖЕН · ДЛИНА 3» and that placement is pinned. This kills classic "hunt mode" and replaces it with something better.

2.5 The player's own board uses the **identical rule with the player as beneficiary** — the machine picks the answer minimising the player's damage and maximising the player's freedom. This is the literal delivery of the seed idea's "машина это легко сделает, а человеку такая комбинаторика сложна". The player never does this work by hand and never chooses a configuration.

2.6 There is **no defensive positioning decision, ever, for either side** — and this is deliberate, not a gap. Since you exist in all consistent configurations at once, there is no state to manage; freedom N is a function of the constraint set alone. Fabricating a "choose which reality to jump into" menu would be fake agency. Player defence is exactly one binary, priced decision per incoming salvo (§5). Say this out loud in the docs.

---

## 3. THE CURRENCY: ФЛЮКС (ФЛ)

3.1 One currency. Both clocks — offense and survival — draw from the same pool. That competition is the game.

3.2 Start **6 ФЛ**. Hard cap **16 ФЛ** (hoarding is a losing line and the cap makes it visibly so).

3.3 **Income, paid at the end of the player's answer phase:**

```
БИТЫ   = log2(N_врага_до / N_врага_после)      // real number, shown to 0.1
ДОХОД  = clamp(2, 8, 2 + round(БИТЫ))
       + 4  за каждый потопленный корабль
       - 1  за каждый свой потопленный корабль (не ниже 0)
```

3.4 This is the loop in one line: **you buy bits with flux and you earn flux with bits.** A shot that teaches you nothing pays nothing. Blind sweeping starves. Typical turn: 1–2 bits → 4 ФЛ. Good turn: 5–6 ФЛ. Kill turn: 8–10 ФЛ.

3.5 Calibration check: winning costs log2(25 000 000) ≈ **24.6 bits**. A miss on a fresh cell removes ~19% of configurations (0.30 bits); a hit removes ~81% (2.4 bits); a kill of a 3-ship pins a placement, ~6.6 bits. At 1.3–1.8 bits/turn the match lands at 16–22 turns. Numbers below are tuned to that.

---

## 4. OFFENSE: THE SALVO

4.1 Exactly one salvo per turn; firing it ends the player phase.

4.2 **A salvo is 1–6 cells, all of which must lie inside a single 3×3 window.** The window is an amber 3×3 reticle the player drags across the enemy board; cells inside it are toggled on/off. Cells already answered cannot be selected.

4.3 Cost: **2·(k−1) ФЛ** → k=1: 0, k=2: 2, k=3: 4, k=4: 6, k=5: 8, k=6: 10.

4.4 Why the 3×3 window (this is load-bearing): globally-free cell selection turns the salvo into "pick the k best cells on the board", which is an optimiser's job, not a human's, and it deletes spatial reading. Locality makes the salvo a **shape** — you learn that the 5-cell X (four corners + centre) is the parity-optimal 3×3 pattern, that it stops being right once two of its cells are proven empty, and that pushing the front sideways is different from pushing it forward. It also makes the min-overlap search fast (§8.3), because clustered cells are cheap to prove dodgeable.

4.5 The book opening is a parity comb: any ship of length ≥2 must occupy at least one cell of a checkerboard colour, and 32 comb-misses are logically impossible for the god to grant (a 2-ship cannot fit in the complementary checkerboard). The comb is *supposed* to be strong — it is this game's 1.e4. Skill is in the deviations, the shapes, and where the flux goes.

---

## 5. DEFENSE: ПРЫЖОК ПО БРАНЕ (the Alcubierre drive)

5.1 The enemy's next salvo is **telegraphed one full turn ahead** as an amber reticle on your board. This is the single most important defensive-fun decision in the design: it converts defence from passive dice into "it is about to land on my last free corner — do I pay 4 ФЛ now or bank it for the Geller field?"

5.2 When the enemy salvo fires, let **D = number of your consistent configurations that avoid ALL cells of the salvo simultaneously.** Partial dodges do not exist. This is exactly why the enemy's escalation to 2- and 3-cell salvos is terrifying.

5.3 Jump price table (offered as one button, «ПРЫЖОК ПО БРАНЕ · 3 ФЛ · ВЕТОК УХОДА 412»):

| D | цена |
|---|---|
| ≥ 100 000 | 1 ФЛ |
| ≥ 5 000 | 2 ФЛ |
| ≥ 200 | 3 ФЛ |
| ≥ 20 | 4 ФЛ |
| ≥ 1 | 5 ФЛ |
| 0 | «УКЛОНЕНИЕ НЕВОЗМОЖНО» — forced |

5.4 The price rises automatically as your reality is pinned down. No fudge factor, no rubber band, no difficulty multiplier: **the cost of survival is a direct readout of how much of you the god already knows.** This is the self-balancing spine of the whole difficulty curve.

5.5 The tiers are coarse *because* D is estimated above the exact-enumeration threshold (§8.2). Estimation error of a few percent never crosses a tier boundary. Document this reason; do not silently hide the estimator.

5.6 Declining is legitimate and often correct early. Answering a hit costs you ~2.4 bits of your own counter; jumping costs ~0.3 bits and 1–5 ФЛ.

---

## 6. THE THREE ABILITIES (each earns its place on a different axis)

### 6.1 ГЕЛЛЕР-ПОЛЕ — 6 ФЛ, 3 charges per match. *Axis: information.*
Place a 3×3 field on the enemy board. The defender must commit to a configuration **minimising** the number of occupied cells inside the region; that count n (0–9) is revealed, and the constraint "exactly n of these 9 cells are occupied" is added permanently. Reality inside the bubble can no longer be re-twisted — the number can never change again, which is literally «пришпилить реальность».
Mechanically this is a Minesweeper number grafted onto Battleship. It typically removes 50–80% of the space (1–2 bits) which partially refunds itself via §3.3, and it makes every subsequent shot inside the region an honest one rather than an adversarial one. Rejected alternative: revealing the region's *contents* — that wins the game for 6 ФЛ. Rejected alternative: pinning without revealing — the god just pins it empty and the player has bought nothing.

### 6.2 ЗАРЯД ЙОГ-СОТОТА — 5 ФЛ, 3 charges per match. *Axis: forced damage and pacing.*
Fire at one cell c. The shot resolves against the possibility space instead of a configuration: **every configuration in which c is empty is annihilated.** If any consistent configuration has a ship at c, the answer is ПОПАДАНИЕ and the god cannot refuse. If none does, the result is «ПУСТОТА ВО ВСЕХ ВЕТВЯХ» — the charge is spent, no refund, but the collapse still pays income.
This is the literal "особый снаряд, которым я могу накрыть сразу несколько альтернативных веток" — it pierces branches instead of occupying one. Its real job is **pacing**: because the god says МИМО whenever it legally can, organic hits do not appear until the board is well saturated, and the Yog charge lets a player manufacture the first hit when they want the thrill or need the tempo. Three charges, no more: it is the sharpest tool in the box.

### 6.3 ДОКАЗАННЫЕ КЛЕТКИ — free, automatic. *Axis: the honesty floor.*
Every turn the engine proves, per unanswered cell, whether a consistent configuration exists that occupies it. Cells occupied in no configuration are marked «ПУСТО»; cells occupied in every configuration are marked as pinned. These are logical consequences of answers already given — charging for them, or hiding them, would be dishonest, and computing them by hand is exactly the combinatorics a human cannot do. Free certainty; paid probability. That line is the design's answer to §7.3.

**Cut abilities and why:** a probability-oracle ("show me whether this salvo is a guaranteed hit before firing") — it replaces the player's judgement with the answer. A decoy/anchor on the player's own board — §2.6 proves it would be a no-op dressed as a choice. A three-candidate reality picker on jump — max-freedom always wins, so it is a fake decision.

---

## 7. THE DEGENERACY CHECK

7.1 **Blind full-board sweep (the big one).** Against a god that answers МИМО whenever it legally can, the naive dominant strategy is "shoot everything until ships stop fitting", which makes skill irrelevant. Killed by three interlocking rules: income is proportional to *bits*, so uninformative shots pay nothing (§3.3); salvo cost rises with k (§4.3); and the enemy's counter is racing yours with an escalating fire rate (§9). A sweep runs out of flux around turn 8 and then cannot dodge.

7.2 **Free-poke hoarding (k=1 costs 0 ФЛ).** Poke one free cell per turn, bank everything, dodge forever. Sums out to ≈0.3 bits/turn × 40 turns = 12 bits, well short of 24.6, while the enemy takes ~0.3 bits/cell × 2–3 cells per turn off you. You lose the turn-40 tiebreak (§10.4). The 16 ФЛ cap makes the hoard visibly worthless. Verified losing line — keep it legal, it is a lesson.

7.3 **Does perfect information trivialise it? Yes — so the heatmap is not shown.** An exact per-cell occupancy probability map reduces the game to "click the brightest square". What is shown instead:
 • the two counters (one scalar, no spatial guidance);
 • **ПРИЗРАЧНЫЕ ФЛОТЫ** — 5 genuinely sampled consistent configurations redrawn every turn as faint 1px silhouettes, each flickering out of phase. Qualitative, honest (they are real branches), unreadable as probabilities. As N falls the ghosts increasingly agree, and the enemy fleet visibly solidifies out of the noise. This is the game's money shot;
 • the proven cells of §6.3.
 A «ПОКАЗЫВАТЬ ТЕПЛОВУЮ КАРТУ» assist lives in the settings drawer, off by default, labelled as a training wheel, and **sets the score to zero**. Honest option, honest price.

7.4 **Always dodge.** Costs ~2 ФЛ/turn out of ~4 income, leaving only k=2 salvos (~0.6 bits/turn) → you need ~40 turns → you lose on the clock.

7.5 **Never dodge.** Your counter falls ~3× faster than it needs to → you lose the race. Both extremes lose; the optimum is a moving allocation. That is the health check on the economy.

7.6 **Salvo-shape solving.** The 5-cell X is a strong default inside an untouched 3×3, and that is acceptable — its value inverts as soon as some of its cells are proven empty or Geller-constrained, which happens every turn. Note it in the docs as a known book move rather than pretending it isn't there.

---

## 8. COMPUTATIONAL CONTRACT (the make-or-break; a programmer needs these exact numbers)

8.1 **Representation.** A placement is a 64-bit mask as two Uint32s. Precompute all 80/96/112 placements per length once. A configuration is a 4-tuple of non-overlapping placements. DFS orders ships longest-first, filters by `mask & E == 0`, and prunes on remaining hit-coverage feasibility. ~10⁷ leaves/sec in plain JS.

8.2 **Counting.** Exact DFS with a node budget of **300 000 nodes (~5–10 ms)**. If it completes, show the exact number. If it does not, estimate with **Knuth's random-path estimator** — walk root-to-leaf multiplying branching factors, 400 samples, ~2 ms, unbiased, few-percent error. Display estimates with a leading «≈» and exact values without. The number therefore becomes exact on its own as the game progresses, which is precisely the collapse fantasy rendered as a typography change.

8.3 **Adversarial answer (§2.2).** Branch-and-bound on |P ∩ S|, placements ordered by ascending overlap with S; the first zero-overlap leaf terminates instantly, which is the common case early. Late game the whole space is small. Budget **2 000 000 nodes (~200 ms)** with the progress-banner idiom lifted from nostromo-gambit («ПЕРЕБОР ВЕТВЕЙ…»). If the budget is exhausted without a proof, the engine returns the best overlap found — which can only *over*-credit the player. Put that in «известные ограничения»; do not pretend it cannot happen.

8.4 **Proven cells (§6.3).** 64 witness searches per turn, each terminating on the first witness, 50 000 nodes each. ~20–50 ms total, chunked behind the banner.

8.5 **Ghost sampling.** 5 near-uniform configurations per turn via branching-weighted random-path DFS with restarts.

8.6 **Boot cost.** The one-time exact census of ~25M leaves is 2–4 s; it is hidden behind the boot typewriter, or simply printed from the verified constant while a test recomputes it.

8.7 **Zero randomness in play.** Everything is deterministic given the seed; the seed decides only the god's tie-breaks, its targeting choices, and which ghosts are drawn. Reuse `src/game/rng.mjs` unchanged. Thematically the seed *is* "which reality the god prefers", which is why it is displayed as «КОД РЕАЛЬНОСТИ» and is replayable.

---

## 9. TURN STRUCTURE, ENEMY, ACTS

9.1 Turn phases:
 1. **РАЗВЕДКА** — counters, ghosts, proven cells, and the enemy's telegraphed reticle on your board update.
 2. **ФАЗА ИГРОКА** — any number of Geller fields and Yog charges while flux allows, in any order, then exactly one salvo, which ends the phase.
 3. **ОТВЕТ** — the god solves §2.2; results animate cell-by-cell, 120 ms stagger; the enemy counter collapses with a descending digit tick; income is paid with a breakdown line.
 4. **ФАЗА ВРАГА** — the telegraphed salvo fires; one jump offer per salvo (§5); damage resolves.
 5. Act check, win/lose check.

9.2 **Enemy targeting is the exact mirror of the player's objective**: it picks the 3×3 window and cell set **minimising D**, your dodging-branch count. Same objective function, same code path, opposite board. It pays no flux — it is a god, and that asymmetry is the theme.

9.3 Act schedule in a single session:

| Акт | Ходы | Огонь врага | Прочее |
|---|---|---|---|
| I «ЗОНД» | 1–6 | 1 клетка | — |
| II «ВНИМАНИЕ» | 7–14 | залп из 2 | учит залпу с принимающей стороны |
| III «ВЗГЛЯД» | 15+ | залп из 3 | Геллер-поле врага по твоей доске на ходах 15 и 22 |

Act transitions use the sliding banner idiom from nostromo-gambit. The enemy's Geller field on your board reveals a 3×3 occupancy count of *your* fleet and pins it — it reuses §6.1 verbatim, no new code, and it is the moment your jump prices jump a tier.

9.4 **Difficulty, five named levels** (data table, not code branches, per house style):
 1 **СПЯЩИЙ** — 1 shot/turn all match; god concedes a hit whenever ≥60% of branches would be hit (only partly adaptive); jump tiers −1.
 2 **ШЕПОТ** — schedule capped at 2; god adversarial only on ties.
 3 **ВЗГЛЯД** — as written above. Default.
 4 **ЗОВ** — +1 cell to every enemy salvo; enemy Geller twice per act.
 5 **АЗАТОТ** — 3-cell salvos from turn 1, jump tiers +1 ФЛ. «Слепой идиот-бог. Он не играет — он просто есть.»
 The "how adaptive is the god" knob at levels 1–2 is the honest way to weaken it: a *less* adaptive god is genuinely easier, whereas a shallower search would just be stranger. Same reasoning as the nostromo `slackCp` decision.

---

## 10. VICTORY, DEFEAT, SCORE

10.1 **Victory:** enemy N reaches 1. Announce «РЕАЛЬНОСТЬ ЗАФИКСИРОВАНА», draw the true fleet solid amber, resolve all ships as destroyed. Never make the player grind out formality shots.

10.2 **Defeat:** your N reaches 1 — «ТЕБЯ НАШЛИ ВО ВСЕХ ВЕТВЯХ». Symmetric.

10.3 These two are the *only* terminal conditions and they are the same condition (§0).

10.4 **Turn 40 hard stop:** lower counter wins; exact tie is a loss. Prevents unbounded stalling; announced from turn 35 as «БОГ ТЕРЯЕТ ИНТЕРЕС · 5».

10.5 **Score:**
```
БАЛЛ = (1000 − 25·ходов − 8·потрачено_флюкса + 150·уцелевших_кораблей) × K
K:  СПЯЩИЙ 0.6 · ШЕПОТ 0.8 · ВЗГЛЯД 1.0 · ЗОВ 1.3 · АЗАТОТ 1.7
Тепловая карта включена → БАЛЛ = 0.
```
Show the breakdown line by line on the end card, never a bare number.

10.6 **Replay drivers:** (a) the score is an efficiency score, so the same match is worth re-solving; (b) **«КОД РЕАЛЬНОСТИ»** — every match runs on a visible seed, and entering the same seed reproduces the god's tie-breaks exactly, so runs are comparable; (c) a **daily seed** derived from the date; (d) five difficulty levels that change the god's *nature*, not its numbers.

---

## 11. WHERE THE FUN ACTUALLY IS (the four skill axes, stated so QA can test them)

1. **Salvo shaping** — maximising bits per flux, and engineering the first forced hit.
2. **Flux allocation** — offense clock vs. survival clock out of one pool; both extremes are proven losing (§7.4, §7.5).
3. **Ability timing** — where to buy a Minesweeper number, when to manufacture a hit.
4. **Reading the ghosts** — a qualitative spatial skill that no exposed number replaces.

The design's central bet: the dopamine of "ПОПАДАНИЕ!" is replaced by the counter collapsing and the ghost fleets converging. Everything in §7.3 and §8.2 exists to make that feedback trustworthy, continuous, and legible. If playtest says the first ten hitless turns feel dead, the lever is the Yog charge count (3 → 4) and the Act I length (6 → 4), in that order — not the god's honesty.

**One audio note** (the reference project has literally none, so this is where the sequel exceeds it): the signature sound is a descending per-digit tick as the counter collapses, pitch mapped to bits collapsed. Two timbres, green and amber, one alert. Created on the «▶ НАЧАТЬ» gesture, toggle in the drawer.

---

## 12. KNOWN LIMITATIONS TO DOCUMENT UP FRONT (house style)

Counts above 300 000 nodes are sampled estimates and are printed with «≈». The adversarial answer has a 2M-node budget; on exhaustion it may credit the player with a hit a perfect god could have dodged. Jump-price tiers are coarse deliberately, because D is estimated. Ships may touch. 10×10 / five-ship mode is not implemented. There is no multiplayer, though nothing in the rules forbids it.

---

I read the proposal against the reference project's actual files and then ran its own numbers.

**The arithmetic that kills it.** Under the god's stated rule, early answers are all misses; a fresh miss removes ~18.75% of the space = 0.30 bits. Apply §3.3 and §4.3:

| k | цена | биты | доход | нетто |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 0.30 | 2 | **+2** |
| 2 | 2 | 0.60 | 3 | +1 |
| 3 | 4 | 0.90 | 3 | −1 |
| 4 | 6 | 1.20 | 3 | −3 |
| 6 | 10 | 1.80 | 4 | −6 |

Net flux is monotonically decreasing in salvo size. The dominant line is the free 1-cell poke — which §7.2 itself proves is a *losing* line, and which never once triggers the salvo-beats-sequential asymmetry that is the whole game (§2.3). Even the bank-and-alpha-strike line yields 3.3 bits per 6 turns ≈ 0.55 bits/turn; 24.6 bits needed → **45 turns against a turn-40 hard stop.** The economy does not merely wobble, it does not close. §3.5's "good turn 5–6 ФЛ" silently assumes hits, and the ruleset guarantees you don't get any.

**The pacing hole.** Min-overlap fails only when the empty set is large enough that 4/3/3/2 cannot be packed. On 8×8 with touching allowed, that's ~35–45 answered cells. At 3 cells/turn the first *organic* hit is turn 12–18 — i.e. never, in an 18–22 turn match. The design knows this (§6.2 "organic hits do not appear until the board is well saturated") and rations the only hit-generator to three charges. So the minute-to-minute experience is: aim a reticle, press fire, read МИМО ×4, watch an 8-digit number go from ≈24 113 662 to ≈23 442 101, read a logarithm, repeat twelve times. That is the spreadsheet.

Full evaluation below.

input.fatal_flaws:
1. THE ECONOMY DOES NOT CLOSE — this is arithmetic, not taste. With cost 2*(k-1) and income clamp(2,8,2+round(bits)), and a fresh miss worth 0.30 bits (12/64 occupancy), net flux per turn is: k=1 -> +2, k=2 -> +1, k=3 -> -1, k=4 -> -3, k=6 -> -6. Net is MONOTONICALLY DECREASING in salvo size. The dominant strategy is the free 1-cell poke, which the design itself proves is a losing line in §7.2, and which never triggers the salvo-beats-sequential asymmetry that is the entire point of the game (§2.3). The design's Nash equilibrium is its own labelled anti-strategy. Even the bank-and-alpha-strike line (bank 5 turns at +2, fire one k=6) yields 3.3 bits / 6 turns = 0.55 bits/turn; 24.6 bits to win = 45 turns against a turn-40 hard stop. You cannot win at the stated numbers. §3.5's "good turn: 5-6 ФЛ" requires 3-4 bits, which requires a hit; the ruleset guarantees no hits. The economy is calibrated for a game the rules forbid.

2. TWELVE TURNS OF МИМО. Min-overlap only fails when the empty set is large enough that 4/3/3/2 cannot be packed. On 8x8 with touching allowed a 4-ship alone has 80 legal runs and killing all of them costs ~30 cells; the real infeasibility threshold is ~35-45 answered cells, i.e. turn 12-18 at 3 cells/turn — in an 18-22 turn match. So the FIRST organic hit arrives at roughly the same time as the win. The god's optimal play deletes Battleship's entire feedback vocabulary. Minute to minute: drag reticle, press fire, read МИМО x4, watch ≈24 113 662 become ≈23 442 101, read a logarithm, repeat. §6.2 rations the only hit-generator to three charges and calls it "pacing". Three scripted moments of drama in twenty turns, all of them purchased. The proposal's central bet — "the dopamine of ПОПАДАНИЕ is replaced by the counter collapsing" — is the bet I would not take. A number going down is idle-game feedback; idle games pair it with exponential growth and constant unlocks, not with a 20-turn deduction puzzle.

3. THE INCOME FORMULA IS A LOGARITHM SHOWN TO THE PLAYER. БИТЫ = log2(N_до/N_после), to 0.1, off a ratio of two 8-digit estimated numbers. No human forms intuition about that. It cannot be planned, only observed after the fact — which makes the primary stated skill axis ("maximise bits per flux", §11.1) a slot machine with a receipt. This single line is the strongest evidence for "spreadsheet, not game".

4. HALF THE GAME IS A CUTSCENE WITH A YES/NO PROMPT. §2.6 admits there is no defensive decision, then rationalises it as anti-fake-agency. The enemy salvo is telegraphed, the dodge-branch count is computed for you, the price is computed for you, and the button says 3 ФЛ. The decision degenerates to "do I have 3 flux". It also kills its own best defensive idea with faulty reasoning: it rejects a branch-picker because "max-freedom always wins", but the score pays +150 per SURVIVING SHIP (§10.5), so branches that differ in shape rather than in N are a real choice and the design already contains the payoff that makes them one.

5. THE GHOSTS ARE A STOCHASTIC HEATMAP WEARING A MASK. 5 samples x 4 ships = up to 60 lit cells over a 64-cell grid. Early game that is uniform mud, not a money shot; it only resolves in the last few turns. Worse, §7.3 bans the heatmap as trivialising and then ships a noisy version of it: a patient player averages the flicker across turns and reconstructs it anyway. The ban therefore punishes the honest player and rewards the one who stares — tedium disguised as skill.

6. THE COMPUTE BUDGET IS UNDER-COSTED WHERE IT MATTERS MOST. §2.2 clause (c) "maximise the resulting N" requires COUNTING the surviving space for each candidate configuration — that is a count per branch-and-bound candidate, not one DFS — and §8.3's 2M-node/200ms budget does not account for it at all. Add §8.4 (64 witness searches x 50k nodes = 3.2M), the D-estimate, and 5 ghost samples, every single turn. The claimed ~50ms is off by an order of magnitude or more.

7. THE COUNTER CAN TICK UP. Knuth's path estimator on a heavily constrained tree has high variance (few-percent is optimistic; 10-30% is realistic on skewed trees). A counter that RISES after a shot is logically impossible and will read as a bug — in the one number on which the entire game's trust rests.

8. YOU DO NOT GET A FINAL BLOW. Victory is N reaching 1: an arithmetic event the game announces for you. §10.1's instinct to skip the "formality shots" is correct and simultaneously an admission that the last 20% is grinding. The turn-40 tiebreak ("exact tie is a loss") is a limp ending and invites boundary turtling. And the efficiency score plus daily seed have nothing to compare against — the house architecture has zero client persistence and no leaderboard.

9. SCOPE. Nostromo Gambit is chess (known) plus ONE novel idea. This is Battleship plus superposition plus a bits-economy plus three abilities plus a telegraph plus an act schedule plus a symmetric superposition board for the player. The hardest thing to communicate — "your own ships also don't exist and the machine dodges for you" — is the one the player must grasp before turn 2. A thousand-indie-game veteran bounces in the first three minutes, not because it is hard but because they cannot tell what they are looking at.

4. THE JUMP PRICE RISES AS YOU ARE PINNED (§5.3, §5.4). Self-balancing difficulty with no rubber band and no hidden multiplier, and the price is literally a readout of how much of you the god already knows. Diegetic and honest. Best economic idea in the doc.

5. THE ENEMY SALVO IS TELEGRAPHED ONE FULL TURN AHEAD (§5.1). Converts defence from dice into a decision and creates the only genuine cross-turn tension in the design.

9. DIFFICULTY AS THE GOD'S ADAPTIVITY, NOT ITS SEARCH DEPTH (§9.4). Correct, and correctly justified by the same reasoning as the nostromo slackCp decision.

10. The descending per-digit tick with pitch mapped to bits collapsed (§11), and «КОД РЕАЛЬНОСТИ» as a visible replayable seed.

input.fixes:
1. GIVE THE GOD A FLUX POOL. This is the one change that fixes flaws 2 and 4 at once and makes the theme better. The god pays to dodge on exactly the same tier table the player pays to jump (§5.3), it earns income the same way, and when it is broke IT BLEEDS — it must concede the hit. Now: hits appear organically from turn 3; the god is legible instead of oracular; the arc becomes "drain the god, then execute it" instead of "shrink a number"; the salvo asymmetry gets sharper because a wide salvo is expensive for the DEFENDER to escape; and §9.2's "it pays no flux, it is a god" trades one theme sentence for the entire pacing problem. Keep the unpaid god as difficulty level 5 АЗАТОТ, where it belongs.

2. RE-PRICE THE SALVO SO THE INTENDED PLAY IS THE AFFORDABLE PLAY. Cost = k-1 (0/1/2/3/4/5), income = 2 + 2*bits, uncapped, no rounding. Then k=4 costs 3 and pays ~4.4 early, net +1.4 with a jump budget on top, and net income now RISES with k up to the point where the god starts conceding. Delete the clamp and the round: they are what flattened the incentive and what made the number unreadable. Show the estimate PROSPECTIVELY on the reticle before firing — «ЗАЛП ИЗ 4 · ЦЕНА 3 ФЛ · ВЕТОК УХОДА У ВРАГА 3 400» — so the player plans instead of audits.

3. FRONT-LOAD THE FIRST HIT. Grant a free Yog charge on turn 1 as «ПЕРВЫЙ КОНТАКТ». The player must see and hear what ПОПАДАНИЕ looks like inside the first ninety seconds, before the twelve turns of МИМО, or they never learn what they are playing for.

4. FIX THE GHOSTS BY SHOWING ONE SHIP AT A TIME. Cycle the ghost layer per hull — «БРАНА · КРЕЙСЕР (4)» — drawing sampled placements of that ship only. Legible instead of mud, thematically stronger (you are watching one hull smear across realities), and structurally NOT a heatmap, so §7.3's ban stops being cosmetic. Let the player pin the cycle to a hull they are hunting.

5. MAKE THE ENDGAME A KILL, NOT A PROOF. When the space collapses below a threshold the fleet is FROZEN, not dead: the god is announced as pinned («РЕАЛЬНОСТЬ ЗАФИКСИРОВАНА»), the ghosts snap into one solid amber fleet, and the player gets one climactic unlimited barrage turn against a target that can no longer move. The whole game the enemy dodges; for ten seconds at the end it cannot. That is the ending the Alcubierre/Azathoth fiction is owed, and it converts §10.1's admitted formality into the payoff.

6. MAKE THE COUNTER TRUSTWORTHY. Track and monotonize log2(N) — never let the displayed value rise. Display 2 significant figures while estimated («≈24 МЛН») and the exact integer once exact, so the typography change alone tells the collapse story. Drive every MECHANIC (jump tiers, income, act triggers) off stable log-N buckets, never off the raw estimate, so estimator noise can never cross a price boundary. Document it in §12.

7. GIVE DEFENCE A SPATIAL VERB. Replace the yes/no jump with "you cannot dodge it all — choose where to take it": offer 2-3 real branches that differ in SHAPE, not in N (one keeps the 4-ship free and pins the 2-ship, another the reverse). §2.6 rejected this on the grounds that max-freedom always wins, which is only true if N is the sole metric — and §10.5 already pays +150 per surviving ship, so it isn't.

Cut the turn-40 tiebreak and let the god's flux pool end the game naturally. Four novel systems on top of a superposed Battleship is at least one too many for a first sitting, and the reference project earned its polish by having exactly one new idea.

9. Two things to move into §12 rather than fix: the 5-cell X being a book move, and the 2M-node budget occasionally over-crediting the player. Both are honest and both are fine.

data.fixes:
1. GIVE THE GOD A FLUX POOL. This is the one change that fixes flaws 2 and 4 at once and makes the theme better. The god pays to dodge on exactly the same tier table the player pays to jump (§5.3), it earns income the same way, and when it is broke IT BLEEDS — it must concede the hit. Now: hits appear organically from turn 3; the god is legible instead of oracular; the arc becomes "drain the god, then execute it" instead of "shrink a number"; the salvo asymmetry gets sharper because a wide salvo is expensive for the DEFENDER to escape; and §9.2's "it pays no flux, it is a god" trades one theme sentence for the entire pacing problem. Keep the unpaid god as difficulty level 5 АЗАТОТ, where it belongs.

2. RE-PRICE THE SALVO SO THE INTENDED PLAY IS THE AFFORDABLE PLAY. Cost = k-1 (0/1/2/3/4/5), income = 2 + 2*bits, uncapped, no rounding. Then k=4 costs 3 and pays ~4.4 early, net +1.4 with a jump budget on top, and net income now RISES with k up to the point where the god starts conceding. Delete the clamp and the round: they are what flattened the incentive and what made the number unreadable. Show the estimate PROSPECTIVELY on the reticle before firing — «ЗАЛП ИЗ 4 · ЦЕНА 3 ФЛ · ВЕТОК УХОДА У ВРАГА 3 400» — so the player plans instead of audits.

3. FRONT-LOAD THE FIRST HIT. Grant a free Yog charge on turn 1 as «ПЕРВЫЙ КОНТАКТ». The player must see and hear what ПОПАДАНИЕ looks like inside the first ninety seconds, before the twelve turns of МИМО, or they never learn what they are playing for.

4. FIX THE GHOSTS BY SHOWING ONE SHIP AT A TIME. Cycle the ghost layer per hull — «БРАНА · КРЕЙСЕР (4)» — drawing sampled placements of that ship only. Legible instead of mud, thematically stronger (you are watching one hull smear across realities), and structurally NOT a heatmap, so §7.3's ban stops being cosmetic. Let the player pin the cycle to a hull they are hunting.

5. MAKE THE ENDGAME A KILL, NOT A PROOF. When the space collapses below a threshold the fleet is FROZEN, not dead: the god is announced as pinned («РЕАЛЬНОСТЬ ЗАФИКСИРОВАНА»), the ghosts snap into one solid amber fleet, and the player gets one climactic unlimited barrage turn against a target that can no longer move. The whole game the enemy dodges; for ten seconds at the end it cannot. That is the ending the Alcubierre/Azathoth fiction is owed, and it converts §10.1's admitted formality into the payoff.

6. MAKE THE COUNTER TRUSTWORTHY. Track and monotonize log2(N) — never let the displayed value rise. Display 2 significant figures while estimated («≈24 МЛН») and the exact integer once exact, so the typography change alone tells the collapse story. Drive every MECHANIC (jump tiers, income, act triggers) off stable log-N buckets, never off the raw estimate, so estimator noise can never cross a price boundary. Document it in §12.

7. GIVE DEFENCE A SPATIAL VERB. Replace the yes/no jump with "you cannot dodge it all — choose where to take it": offer 2-3 real branches that differ in SHAPE, not in N (one keeps the 4-ship free and pins the 2-ship, another the reverse). §2.6 rejected this on the grounds that max-freedom always wins, which is only true if N is the sole metric — and §10.5 already pays +150 per surviving ship, so it isn't.

8. CUT ONE WHOLE SYSTEM. Ship it with the acts table (§9.3) OR the score multipliers (§10.5) OR the third ability, not all three. Cut the turn-40 tiebreak and let the god's flux pool end the game naturally. Four novel systems on top of a superposed Battleship is at least one too many for a first sitting, and the reference project earned its polish by having exactly one new idea.

9. Two things to move into §12 rather than fix: the 5-cell X being a book move, and the 2M-node budget occasionally over-crediting the player. Both are honest and both are fine.
